Niyara Bund Restorer

Team ACE, University of Moratuwa. Market concept, 8 October 2026.

Niyara නියර

A one-pass bund restorer for the RV125 two-wheel tractor

Each bund is built to one standard shape once. After that, Niyara restores it every season in one pass per face. Two knives shave the old surface, a rotor throws fresh mud from beside the bund onto it, and a spinning dish trowels it into a sealed 30 mm coat. Every number on this page is a first estimate, to be replaced by the field measurements in the test plan below.

    One pass, front to back

    The tractor walks in the field beside the bund. Everything behind it happens in this order, on one frame, at 10 to 20 m per minute.

    1. Read the bund

      The ski rides the old bund top. Every tool works at a fixed height above it, however deep the wheels sink.

    2. Shave

      Two knives take 15 to 20 mm off the top and the face. Grass and roots come off and crab holes open up.

    3. Win and throw

      The rotor cuts about 20 L of mud per metre from beside the toe and throws it back over itself onto the face and top.

    4. Trowel

      The dish spins faster than it rolls. It drags the mud into the bund, presses it and smears a sealed skin, hardest at the waterline.

    5. Leave a finished bund

      A 30 mm coat sits on the standard profile. The shallow trench beside it is levelled by the next puddling.

    Your teammates' compaction roller lives on as the dish trowel. It keeps the drum-and-flare idea, but the dish is now driven faster than it rolls and sized to the standard bund. The wire brush, the concave disc and the drag collector are retired: in wet clay the brush clogs, and the passive parts cannot lift mud onto the bund.

    Why this design

    The RV125 has spare shaft power but very little spare pull: about 1.2 to 1.4 kN before the cage wheels slip. So every part that does real work on the mud is driven or rolling, and nothing large is dragged.

    Going to market

    Who buys

    Contractors who already hire out two-wheel tractors for ploughing and rotavating. Bund restoring becomes one more paid job each season. Farmers who own an RV125 are the second market.

    First season

    Sell the standardising as a service: the same tractor with a forming template shapes each bund once. The farmer keeps a plywood profile template to check bunds every year.

    Parts

    Standard tiller L-blades, roller chain, sealed bearings, flat bar and pipe. All are stocked wherever two-wheel tractors are repaired.

    Price

    Under Rs 200,000 in batches. The payback depends on the price a contractor can charge per metre, so measure the real work rate in test D1 before quoting it.

    Tests and results

    Run the stages in order. Each test answers one question that would otherwise be answered by a failed prototype. Type the numbers into the card as you measure; everyone this page is shared with sees them, and Claude can read them to finalise the design.

    Connecting to the results log…

    Field kit for stage A

    • Tape, straight edge and a phone inclinometer app
    • 1 L tin and a kitchen scale
    • 50 kg crane or spring scale, and a luggage scale
    • 1 m rod marked every 10 mm
    • Stopwatch, and a strobe or tachometer app for rpm
    • The printed fall cone from the B kit

    Print list for stage B (PETG, 4 walls, 40 % infill)

    • Rotor 1:4: tip circle Ø105 × 70 mm, 4 flanges, 8 L-blades 3 mm thick (or cut from 1 mm steel), M8 shaft, two 608 bearings
    • Volute hood 1:4: radius 59 mm, 85 mm long, two halves with a 30 mm outlet lip; plus an open cover to compare
    • Dish 1:4: internal drum Ø45 × 40 with cone to Ø145 over 29 mm; external drum Ø45 × 90 with cone to Ø195 over 43 mm
    • Bund form 1:4: 50 mm high, 62.5 mm top, 60° faces, four 250 mm segments with slots for catch trays
    • Coupons 50 × 50 mm: smooth, 1 mm ribs, 2 mm dimples, 3 mm domes
    • Fall cone: 30° tip, 80 g with nut pockets, and a release stand
    • Full-size profile templates, internal and external, in four pieces each (or cut from plywood)
